subject: Possible Bug? - Theta Parameterization in Parameter Table Form

messages.author: 0254ffaf93eb3d27
messages.subject: Possible Bug? - Theta Parameterization in Parameter Table Form
parts:
I noticed an peculiarity when I was experimenting with parameter tables for multiple groups. I simulated the attached data, which consists of two groups. I ran the following SEM:

model1<-'

f1 =~ 0.85*x1 + x2 + c(l1.3,l1.3)*x3 + x4 + c(l1.5,l1.5)*x5 + x6
f2 =~ 0.55*y1 + c(l2.2,l2.2)*y2 + c(l2.3,l2.3)*y3 + c(l2.4,l2.4)*y4

f2 ~ f1

f1 ~ c(0,NA)*1
f2 ~ c(0,NA)*1

f1 ~~ f1
f2 ~~ f2

x1 ~~ c(1,NA)*x1
x2 ~~ c(1,1)*x2
x3 ~~ c(1,NA)*x3
x4 ~~ c(1,1)*x4
x5 ~~ c(1,NA)*x5
x6 ~~ c(1,1)*x6

x1 | c(a,a)*t1 + c(b,b)*t2
x2 | t1 + t2
x3 | c(c,c)*t1 + c(d,d)*t2
x4 | t1 + t2
x5 | c(e,e)*t1 + c(f,f)*t2
x6 | t1 + t2

y1 ~~ c(1,NA)*y1
y2 ~~ c(1,NA)*y2
y3 ~~ c(1,NA)*y3
y4 ~~ c(1,NA)*y4

y1 | c(g,g)*t1 + c(h,h)*t2 + c(i,i)*t3 + c(j,j)*t4
y2 | c(k,k)*t1 + c(l,l)*t2 + c(m,m)*t3 + c(n,n)*t4
y3 | c(o,o)*t1 + c(p,p)*t2 + c(q,q)*t3 + c(r,r)*t4
y4 | c(s,s)*t1 + c(t,t)*t2 + c(u,u)*t3 + c(v,v)*t4

'



First using the syntax above directly:

out1<-sem(model=model1,data=sampledata,parameterization = "theta",group="group")

In which case it works fine. However I then tried to do the same using parameter tables instead:

partable<-lavaanify(model1,ngroups = 2)
out1<-sem(model=model1,data=sampledata,parameterization = "theta",group="group")

At which point I get the following error:

Error in MLIST$delta[, 1L] <- sqrt(1/tmp) :
  incorrect number of subscripts on matrix
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50) #The warnings are per standard; they arise due to blank cells in the bivariate frequency tables


If I remove the theta parameterization argument it works fine (though of course not the result I need). I need to be able to manipulate the parameter table directly as I'm running a Monte Carlo with a number of different combinations of parameters.

Any thoughts on why this might be happening?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Possible Bug? - Theta Parameterization in Parameter Table Form
parts:
partable<-lavaanify(model1,ngroups = 2)
out1<-sem(model=model1,data=sampledata,parameterization = "theta",group="group")

?lavaanify

The default for lavaanify() is parameterization = "delta", which is why it works when you run the model that way in your call to sem().  It should give no warning if you run:

partable <- lavaanify(model1, ngroups = 2, parameterization = "theta")
out1 <- sem(model = model1, data = sampledata, parameterization = "theta", group = "group")


Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Possible Bug? - Theta Parameterization in Parameter Table Form
parts:
On 04/22/2015 03:18 PM, UCLU wrote:
> Thank you, however as far as I can tell theta parameterization does not
> affect the default parameters set during the lavaanify function. That is:
>
> |
> lavaanify(model1,ngroups =2)==lavaanify(model1,ngroups
> =2,parameterization ="theta")

but you did not provide enough information to lavaanify(): it needs to
know which variables should be considered as 'ordered'! This information
comes from the varTable argument. This varTable is in fact the 'ov' slot
of fit@Data:

fit@Data@ov

In addition, you also need to set the auto.th and auto.delta arguments.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Possible Bug? - Theta Parameterization in Parameter Table Form
parts:
On 05/13/2015 12:40 AM, UCLU wrote:
> Hi Yves, thank you. I am puzzled as to the use of the varTable argument
> as the model specifies via setting up threshold parameters that all
> observed variables are in fact ordered?

That is correct. If you have all the thresholds in the model syntax,
there is no need for the varTable.


> Similarly so for auto.th?

Indeed.

> Also, with auto.delta - since the parameterization is theta surely this
> necessitates that auto.delta is set to the default of FALSE?

No. You still need them. They are just not free parameters (but a
function of other parameters). But we still need those values.

As for the lavaanify() function in general, the easiest way to use this
is to set the flag auto = TRUE, and you should get identical results as
if you would call the sem() function:

partable <- lavaanify(model1, ngroups = 2, parameterization = "theta",
auto = TRUE)

Yves.
